## Final hypothesis

**The Economics domain is where the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies.**

Using the strict criterion that an O/R pair counts as "majority male in both" when `authors_male.o > 0.5` **and** `authors_male.r > 0.5` (at the O/R-pair level, 141 pairs, with each multi-lab replication's ratio taken as the mean across its lab rows):

| domain | pairs (n) | mean authors_male.o | mean authors_male.r | pairs majority-male in both | share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Economics** | 18 | 0.870 | 0.837 | 10 | **0.556** |
| Cognitive | 49 | 0.711 | 0.518 | 18 | 0.367 |
| Social | 74 | 0.658 | 0.486 | 20 | 0.270 |

So over half of Economics O/R pairs have both an original and a replication author team that is majority male (10 of 18, 55.6%), the highest share across domains, and Economics also has the highest mean male-author ratio for **both** the original (0.870) and the replication (0.837) studies. The ranking Economics > Cognitive > Social is stable under both sensitivity checks — row-level unit (99/241 = 41.1% Cognitive, 201/668 = 30.1% Social, Economics unchanged at 55.6%) and the inclusive `>= 0.5` threshold (Economics 83.3% vs Cognitive 61.2% vs Social 56.8%). The only caveat is precision: Economics rests on just 18 pairs (Wilson 95% CI for the share 0.337–0.754), so the estimate is noisier than for Cognitive (49) and Social (74), but no variant or metric puts any other domain ahead of it.

payload.hypothesis: Economics is the domain in which the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies: 10 of 18 Economics O/R pairs (55.6%) have authors_male.o > 0.5 and authors_male.r > 0.5 (strict criterion), the highest share versus Cognitive (18/49 = 36.7%) and Social (20/74 = 27.0%), and Economics also shows the highest mean male-author ratios for both original (0.870) and replication (0.837) studies. The Economics > Cognitive > Social ranking held under both sensitivity variants (row-level unit and inclusive >= 0.5 threshold). Caveat: Economics rests on only 18 pairs, so its estimate is less precise than the other domains.
payload.workflow: Loaded the primary dataset (927 rows, 141 unique O/R pairs). Defined majority-male-in-both as authors_male.o > 0.5 AND authors_male.r > 0.5 at O/R-pair level, with each multi-lab (ml1/ml3) pair's replication ratio taken as the mean of its lab rows. Computed per-discipline share and counts of qualifying pairs plus mean ratios, then ran two sensitivity variants: (a) row-level unit (each lab replication counted) and (b) inclusive >= 0.5 threshold. Economics led on all metrics in all variants; exact counts/percentages and Wilson 95% CI computed; no missing values required handling.
